subject: is it possible to include radial distances in distance sampling with line transects

messages.author: 2f9d735a39df8472
messages.subject: is it possible to include radial distances in distance sampling with line transects
parts:
Hi all,

I am trying to use distance sampling as a method to analyze bird abundance data from line transects (using RStudio, not the program Distance). I have 15 line transects each repeated 3 times with the design being that 2 observers started at the mid-point and walk out to the end point. The 15 transects are from 3 plots with 5 sites (Study.Area) (each site being a different treatment that is repeated among plots). So I have 5 treatments repeated 3 times.

I understand that for line transects, the "distance" used is the perpendicular distance of the bird observed to the observer. But I have estimates of the radial distance of the bird to the center based on distance of the observer to the center, bearing of the bird from the observer, and estimated distance of the bird from the observer. 

I want to know how abundance might change by treatment (Region.Label) with increased distance from the center, hence why I have these radial distances. But when I use formula = ~radial_distance, I get errors. 

Is this question achievable with distance sampling? 

Other questions that are slightly related. Can I include site as a random variable in these analyses? Can I look at an interaction between treatment and radial distance, or include interactions at all?

Previous students I know have used GLMMs to estimate abundance in the same study system as I am referring to, but I want to use distance sampling if I can as it seems to be very popular for estimating abundance and I appreciate the inclusion of detectability as my transects were performed by observers of different bird ID skill levels. 

I am happy to include some of my code, or show what my raw data looks like if these questions don't make sense or need to be clarified. I am relatively new to R and performing statistical analyses, and all my work using distance sampling has been self-taught, so any help is greatly appreciated. Thanks in advance!!

Johanna

messages.subject: Re: {Suspected Spam} [distance-sampling] is it possible to include radial distances in distance sampling with line transects
parts:
Johanna

I think I understand your study design with 5 treatments therefore you would like to estimate bird abundance for each of these treatments.  I think you have three transects for each of the treatments, which is a small level of replication on which to base your abundance estimates.

I'm troubled by your statement "how abundance might change by treatment (Region.Label) with increased distance from the center".  This makes me think you believe abundance changes as a function of distance along the transect (transects being walked outward from the centre).  This makes your problem difficult for distance sampling because a) estimation of abundance requires multiple transects and b) using ~radial.distance in the detection function model simply states that detectability changes as a function of distance to the centre.  If both detectability and abundance are changing from the centre, they are confounded and analysis is not possible without further data.

Distance sampling does account for imperfect detectability, but to do so, sufficient detections need to be made and sufficient spatial replication of transects are needed for each stratum (treatment) for which you wish to estimate abundance.  My sense is that your design does not lend itself to analysis via distance sampling.
